title: Routed SwiGLU experts over a slot store of expert bundles on BF16 tensor cores, every stored format, decode rows and prompt chunks with the same bits

decode.what: items of 8 routes (decode rows): a warp owns row tiles of one expert, 4-bit codes decoded through a shared byte table, the routes' operands read straight from global memory, weights DEPTH blocks ahead, 128 bytes of a row a request (READ)

WARPS.what: warps a block, each owning TILES row tiles of one expert

TILES.what: MMA row tiles a warp owns (gate/up: 8 inter rows each, down: 16 output rows), sharing each B fragment

DEPTH.what: 64-k blocks of weights in flight a warp (0: the format's depth, 2-6 by format and tiles)

READ.what: how a warp asks for its weights: 1 a 64-k block at a time (32 bytes of a row of a 4-bit format, 64 of FP8), 2 128 bytes of a row at a time (4 blocks of a 4-bit format, 2 of FP8; BF16 is 128 bytes a block either way), 0 the launch's choice: 2 for a pass of 256 k values or more

yardstick.library: FlashInfer grouped GEMM (flashinfer.grouped_mm.grouped_mm_bf16, cuDNN MoE backend) on the pass's weights widened to BF16 once, the routes' inputs gathered in expert order and (gate/up) the SwiGLU in torch: no library takes every stored format against BF16 inputs one pass at a time

prompt.what: items of 32 routes (prompt chunks): the routes' operands staged in shared memory by cp.async, the next chunk landing while the current one computes; each weight fragment feeds four n-tiles

DEPTH.what: 64-k blocks of weights in flight a warp (0: the format's depth, 2-6 by format and tiles)

CHUNK.what: k values of the item's inputs staged a pass by cp.async (two halves of shared memory, at most 48 KiB)

fp4-decode.what: nvfp4 W4A4 items of 8 routes (decode rows) on the block-scaled FP4 tensor cores (mma.sync kind::mxf4nvf4 m16n8k64, the sm_120 family): every route's inputs quantized once by crit's declared NVFP4 quantizer at its expert's input scale (E2M1 codes, UE4M3 block scales), the weights' own codes and scales the A operand, K cut into k_parts(K) parts at fixed 128-k block boundaries (4 from 2,048 k, 2 from 512, else 1: K's alone), one MMA chain an output a part over its 64-blocks in order, the parts' sums added in part order in FP32 (mma_experts.cu's mainloop, its FP4 atom); a part a warp, the parts added through shared memory, the routes' operands read straight from global memory, DEPTH weight steps (128 k) in flight; the intermediate quantized the same way at the down's input scale in the gate/up epilogue (another arithmetic than the BF16 path's W4A4: the same operands, the tensor core's own sums)

WARPS.what: warps a block, each owning TILES row tiles of one expert

TILES.what: MMA row tiles a warp owns (gate/up: 8 inter rows each, run in pairs: a warp holds the intermediate's 16-row blocks; down: 16 output rows), sharing each B fragment

DEPTH.what: weight steps of 128 k (64 bytes of a row) in flight a warp

FETCH.what: how a lane reads a weight step (128 k, 64 bytes of a row) and the route's: 0 its 16 contiguous bytes, then a quad transpose into its fragment words; 1 its four fragment words directly (4-byte loads 16 bytes apart): the same registers and bits, fewer instructions a step; the default takes 1 at one token (RTX 5090: 2048 x 768 FP4 1.34x, FP8 1.17x a layer, level on 4096 x 1536) and 0 from 2 tokens, where the transpose's one 16-byte load a row is as fast or faster

yardstick.library: FlashInfer grouped GEMM (flashinfer.grouped_mm.grouped_mm_bf16, cuDNN MoE backend) on the pass's weights widened to BF16 once, as the BF16 path's benches: no library takes grouped NVFP4 W4A4 one pass at a time

fp4-prompt.what: nvfp4 W4A4 items of 32 or 64 routes (prompt chunks) with fp4-decode's bits: the same parts, chains and part-order sum an output (a warp runs the parts one after another, adding each into a second accumulator), the routes' codes and scales staged in shared memory a CHUNK at a time by cp.async (the next landing while the current one computes), each weight fragment feeding the item's 4 or 8 n-tiles
